description: The window showing the server's own SPA. Its page is served by the subshell-server this app manages, so it is treated as REMOTE content: it may raise the assistant, drop its own title bar, show one notification, drag its window, open a page of THIS server in the system browser — and, as the ONE deliberate exception to 'nothing that touches the service', switch who runs the server. That exception is argued in docs/security.md: a page already holding the admin restart route can do worse than move the server between two supervisors, and the assistant window that used to carry the act read as a bug. The browser one is not a second exception: it takes a PATH, refuses anything that could be a host, and joins it onto this window's own loopback origin — so it opens the server the page is already running in, which a person can do by typing the address. Everything else that touches the CLI is absent by construction, not by convention.
